Package ui

Class ReportScreen

java.lang.Object
ui.ReportScreen
public class ReportScreen extends Object
JavaFX controller for the Analytics & Reports screen (ReportScreen.fxml).

This screen is read-only. It executes all six management reports against the live database on initialisation and displays the results in six non-editable TextArea widgets. All reports are scoped to the previous calendar month (except Report 1, which is all-time).

Reports are loaded eagerly in initialize() — there is no manual refresh button. To re-run the reports, the user can navigate away and return to this screen.

Reports displayed

  1. reportOutput1 — Most popular suite class (all-time reservation count)
  2. reportOutput2 — Hotels with no experience bookings last month
  3. reportOutput3 — Top concierge by total experience value last month
  4. reportOutput4 — Guests who reserved but booked no experiences last month
  5. reportOutput5 — Available (unreserved) suites per hotel last month
  6. reportOutput6 — Guest suite spend last month (checked-out only)

The controller is instantiated and injected by the JavaFX FXMLLoader when ReportScreen.fxml is loaded.

  • Method Details

    • initialize

      public void initialize()
      Called automatically by the JavaFX runtime after all @FXML fields have been injected.

      Instantiates ReportsDAO and immediately calls loadAllReports() to populate all six output areas. If the DAO cannot be created (e.g. database unreachable), all six output areas are set to an error message via showError(String).

    • loadAllReports

      private void loadAllReports()
      Executes all six report queries in sequence and writes results to the corresponding TextArea widgets.

      Each report is fetched independently. A failure in one report does not prevent the others from loading — however, the current implementation wraps all six calls in a single try-catch, so a failure in any one report will short-circuit the remaining ones and display a global error via showError(String). Consider splitting into per-report try-catches for more granular error isolation.

      Multi-row results (Reports 2, 4, 5, 6) are joined with newline characters before being set on the text area.

    • showError

      private void showError(String message)
      Sets all six report output areas to a prefixed error message. Each area is guarded against null to tolerate partial FXML injection.
      Parameters:
      message - the error message to display; prefixed with "ERROR: "
